scenario.title: Pirate Island
scenario.summary: The main scenario: five factions on one tropical island, Michael alone on the beach.

histories: She wraps seeds in scraps of linen and labels each packet. Some are from trees the island no longer has. She intends that to be a temporary problem.
She learned to track deer along the old canopy paths. Since the wreck, she has become distracted by the tracks of machines that do not quite walk like animals.
She carries water to young roots after her watch. She can tell which channel feeds which tree, and remembers when every one of them ran clear.
actor_def.elven.bow_warden.recruitment_offer: I can walk beside you without forgetting what I protect. Make room for me, Michael. I choose to see where this road leads.
companion_responses: Mind the little packets. You may put your coat on them, but not your boots. Someday we can argue in their shade.
Your machines leave the strangest tracks. I was following one before I met you. Now I appear to be following its inventor.
We have time to fill the flask. Listen—the water is clean here. Stay a moment, Michael. Not every stop needs to be a battle.

histories: A former dock guard who enlisted for regular wages. He keeps his boots polished even in the island mud.
A cooper's son who knows how a sound barrel should ring. He counts supply casks before he counts enemy flags.
He learned to read from discarded shipping notices. He still saves every letter that reaches the garrison.
She guarded a survey party before joining the garrison. Their unfinished map still tempts her more than another season of watching the same gate.
A gunsmith taught her to fit a flint and listen for a faulty lock. She volunteered for the island expecting a chance to make something of her own.
She once brought two lost sentries home through a storm. The officer who claimed the credit never learned their names. She did.
actor_def.colonial.line_marine.recruitment_offer: I know my duty, Michael. I also know I can choose another life. Give me a place in your crew, and I'll come willingly.
companion_responses: I've brought the map. Most of the interesting parts are blank. You can carry the compass; I'll tell you when you're holding it upside down.
Let me see that lock before you fire it again. There. Now it might hit what you're looking at. Try looking at the target, Captain.
I kept my musket. You kept your word. That's a good beginning. And if either of us gets lost, the other comes looking.

histories: He came aboard as a cook's helper and stayed for a share of the prize money. He can stretch a pot of stew remarkably far.
A former ferry hand who knows the price of a broken rope. He checks his knots twice and his captain's promises three times.
He once repaired fishing nets for a living. He wants enough gold to own a boat whose course is his to choose.
She learned her knots on a fishing boat. Her present captain has been keeping more than his share, and she is looking for a crew that keeps its word.
She can mend a sail and hold a narrow gangway. After another missing share of the prize money, she has decided her next captain will answer questions.
She joined the quay crew for honest shares of dishonest work. She has kept the accounts, and the numbers have stopped adding up.
actor_def.pirates.deckhand.recruitment_offer: A fair share, and a captain who keeps his word. If that's your crew, Michael, I'll join it.
companion_responses: Your crew now, Captain. Give me a sound rope and a straight answer and we'll get along beautifully. Here—your knot's slipping. Let me.
I used to mend their sails and hold their gangway. They still thought they could short my share. You listened when I spoke, Michael. Don't stop now that I'm here.
I've kept my old accounts. Leaving that crew doesn't make their sums add up. But today I'd rather walk beside you than spend another hour counting what they owe me.

histories: She guarded silk caravans before the island routes became battle lines. She can spot a false trail, but still believes a promise ought to mean something.
Her family traded rice from a narrow riverboat. She learned her spear work keeping thieves off the cargo, and her balance walking the gunwale.
She carried messages between watch posts until her superiors began calling every retreat a victory. She would rather follow someone who admits when he is lost.
actor_def.eastern_fox_people.spear_skirm.recruitment_offer: I can choose my own road, Michael. Make room beside you and I'll take it.
companion_responses: Keep your promises, Captain. I'll keep an eye on the road. And occasionally on you.
You walk like a man who trusts the ground to stay put. Come aboard a riverboat sometime. I'll teach you.
Wrong turning. Don't look so wounded—I'm still coming with you.

histories: Before the shrine, he copied cargo tallies. He still writes numbers in the margins of his prayers.
He used to mend lamps along the waterfront. Since the dreams began, he cannot sleep beside an unlit wick.
He followed a missing brother's trail to the shrine. He remembers the search more clearly than what he found.
She copied tide records before the shrine offered access to its older charts. She keeps a second notebook for the entries that change while nobody is looking.
She heard a childhood melody coming from the drowned shrine. She still wants to know who was singing, but no answer is worth surrendering every other part of her life.
She joined the shrine to study the strange minerals washed up after storms. Her pockets still hold labeled samples, ordinary shells and one pebble she refuses to throw away.
actor_def.cthulhu.drowned_cultist.recruitment_offer: I came here looking for answers. I've heard enough. If there's a place beside you, Michael, I'm choosing to leave.
companion_responses: You can read the second notebook. If an entry changes, tell me. I would rather have someone beside me who notices.
I still know the rites. Knowing them doesn't mean I owe the shrine my life. Come on. I'd like to hear a different song tonight.
That one's just a pebble, Captain. Not everything in my pockets is a portent. Hold this jar while I find the interesting one.

island.backstory: Captain of the Handsome Jack. Shipwreck survivor and inventor.

art.accessibilityDescription: An adult human inventor-captain with a lean 1850s American frontier silhouette: weathered slouch hat, dark sea coat, boots, brass echo compass, compact boiler pack, steam repeating carbine, experimental sidearm and cutlass.

metadata.narrativeAuthoringRule: Every protagonist and heroine must have a personal history, a present pressure, a household life, a specific relationship progression, and a contribution outside combat before the character is production-ready.
notes: Full canonical name: Captain Michael Corrigan. Title cards and ordinary dialogue use Michael; Captain Corrigan is the formal or professional address.
Michael is visible in every battle roster. This first Betty-focused prototype does not expose his Echo command deck yet.

Before the island he commanded the Handsome Jack, an old tea cutter already obsolete by the time of Commodore Perry's expedition. A later owner fitted it with a steam engine too powerful and poorly balanced for the hull.

The engine's weight and thrust made the Handsome Jack fast in fair water. In the typhoon that wrecked the expedition, the overloaded machinery and unstable hull tore the ship apart. Michael survived the wreck; the Handsome Jack did not.

His player-facing silhouette is American frontier circa the 1850s: lean, weathered, practical, with a slouch hat and gun belt. He reads as a cowboy who has also survived a sea wreck, not as a uniformed naval officer.

His loadout is steampunk. The Handsome Jack steam carbine, experimental sidearm, cutlass, compact boiler pack, brass tools and echo compass must look like one repairable field kit rather than unrelated costume props.

He is a genius inventor. Each heroine teaches him a real method from her own discipline; he adapts those methods into expedition hardware with her knowledge and approval. Their relationships drive shared discovery and household projects, never extraction of an ability from a passive companion.
Echo abilities are mechanically distinct from heroine bond skills and must be authored as their own combat records before they become player commands.
The paper card is a contract for rail scale, silhouette and costume read; it is not a substitute for final character art.

island.backstory: A surgeon's mate who learned to fight because the wounded kept ending up on the wrong side of the boarding line. She would still rather stop a blow than land one.
island.recruitmentOffer: I have patched up better men than the ones I sail with. Take me along, Michael, and I will keep you standing long enough to finish whatever you are building.
island.companionResponse: Hold still. You have been favouring that shoulder since the reef and pretending you have not.

art.accessibilityDescription: A slender, lightly built adult field medic with freckles, bright green eyes and auburn curls, wearing a cropped teal pirate-physician outfit and carrying an oversized bronze-and-glass medical war mace.

notes: Canonical combat job: protection through physical intervention and field medicine.

Betty must read as cute and sexy before she reads as realistic. The approved visual language is premium adult anime-fantasy: bright eyes, freckles, auburn curls, confident flirtatious energy, cropped medic blouse, fitted teal corset, short field shorts and tall boots.
Locked body direction: slight agile adult frame, modest small chest, narrow hips, fine waist and long lean legs. Do not drift toward voluptuous, heavy-hourglass or physically bulky anatomy.
Current Magnific references are component references only; no single image is an approved production identity sheet.

island.backstory: A garrison gunner who kept the fort's ranging tables in her own hand because the issued ones were wrong and nobody above her wanted to hear it. She has been quietly right for three years.
island.recruitmentOffer: Your carbine throws left at distance and you have been compensating by feel. I can give you the numbers instead, Michael. Take me with you and stop guessing.
island.companionResponse: Measure it twice before you build it. I have watched what happens to men who trust a number they did not check.

art.accessibilityDescription: An adult colonial gunner with a compact, square-shouldered build, dark hair pinned back under a forage cap, powder-marked hands, a brass ranging glass on a lanyard and a practical uniform coat stripped of insignia.

metadata.competenceDomain: Ballistics, ranging and artillery survey. She turns Michael's guesswork about distance, drop and fortification into measured numbers he can build against.
notes: Canonical competence: she teaches Michael measurement. His inventions gain accuracy he cannot reach by intuition.
She left no dramatic betrayal behind her; her grievance is bureaucratic and specific, which is why she is willing to be asked.
Placed with the colonial powers so the player meets her as an ordinary garrison soldier before learning she is the one who fixed the tables.

Authored notable, not yet a full heroine: she carries identity, competence and recruitment content, and the seven-skill hero kit is the declared gate for promoting her to kind heroine. The authority allows this explicitly -- historical seven-rank skill prototypes are not a universal NPC requirement -- and it is what keeps a roster of dozens affordable.

island.backstory: A warden of the island's water channels who can name which spring feeds which grove and remembers when every one of them ran clear. Several no longer do, and she knows exactly how far the wrongness has spread inland.
island.recruitmentOffer: I can tell you which ground is going bad and how fast, and you are the first person here who has asked instead of arguing. Make room beside you, Michael, and I will show you the whole map of it.
island.companionResponse: The water tastes different this far east. Do not drink from the low channels until I have looked at them.

art.accessibilityDescription: An adult elven water warden, tall and long-limbed, with river-grey eyes, dark braided hair threaded with reed cord, bare forearms marked by sun and water, a slim recurved bow and a belt of stoppered sampling vials.

metadata.competenceDomain: Island ecology and hydrology. She reads the spread of the cult's corruption through water and growing things, turning a vague dread into a mapped, dated front Michael can act on.
notes: Canonical competence: she teaches Michael to read the island itself as evidence, which is the backbone of her investigation lane.
Her stake is concrete and local: named channels she can prove are changing, not a prophecy.
Placed with the elves so her knowledge arrives attached to a faction with its own opinion about the water.

island.backstory: A wayfinder who crossed to this island by star-reckoning and has been quietly correcting her own charts ever since, because the stars over the reef do not sit where her tradition says they should.
island.recruitmentOffer: Something here is wrong with the sky, and I would rather be wrong about it beside someone who builds things than alone with my charts. Make room, Michael.
island.companionResponse: I marked our route back before we set out. You would be astonished how few people think to.

art.accessibilityDescription: An adult fox-people wayfinder with russet ears and tail, a lean travelling build, dark eyes, a weathered travelling coat over eastern layered cloth, a slim spear used as a walking stave and a lacquered case of rolled charts.

metadata.competenceDomain: Navigation, cartography and star-reckoning. She turns the island's geography and the wrongness overhead into routes, bearings and a record of what has changed since she arrived.
notes: Canonical competence: she teaches Michael to navigate and to notice that the sky itself is evidence, which links her lane to the campaign clock rather than to combat.
Her charts are a running record, so her contribution compounds over the campaign instead of being spent once.
Placed with the eastern fox people, whose spear skirmishers already carry the eastern art direction the visual authority approved.

stage.shipwrecked.objective: Michael has the wreck, a workshop of ideas, and no one to share them with.

stage.supported.objective: Someone chose to stand with him. The island is a little less enormous now.

stage.recruiting.objective: Michael can stand beside up to four women. He has room to spare.

stage.complete.objective: Four women stand with him now, whatever that will come to mean.

stage.rumors.objective: Something is wrong out past the reef. The colonial patrols dismiss it as superstition.

stage.confirmed.objective: The drowned shrine is growing. Whatever is down there is no longer content to wait.

stage.colonial_response.objective: The colonials have finally turned their guns on the water. It has begun.

stage.five_factions.objective: Five factions bleed this island dry. Michael counts himself lucky no one has found the wreck yet.

stage.first_fall.objective: The colonial banner came down over the fort. One less flag flying, one less patrol to dodge.

stage.untouched.objective: The wreck still holds everything Michael could not carry ashore the night it ran aground.

stage.stripped.objective: He has stripped her to the ribs. Whatever he builds on this island, he builds out of the ship that failed him.

stage.hearsay.objective: Michael knows the cult's ground only from what frightened people have said about it.

stage.witnessed.objective: He stood on it and looked at it himself. Some things are worse for being confirmed.

leads.observation: I have been counting the dead we pass. It is not the same men doing the dying each week -- the factions are eating their own recruits faster than they can raise them. Whatever is out here, it is grinding them down, and nobody at the fort will say the word for it.
leads.request: You have one pair of hands and so do I. Tell me whether we spend the next stretch getting strong or getting clear, because we cannot do both.

interpretations.claim: We dig in. Build here, take what the wreck still owes us, and be the thing that is still standing when they have finished each other off.
We stay light and stay moving. Anything we build is something we have to defend, and I would rather be somewhere else when it comes for us.

leads.observation: The low channels east of the shrine have gone brackish in eleven days. Not drying -- turning. I have the dates and I have the taste of it, and I would rather be wrong in front of you than quiet in front of them.
leads.request: I want to know whether we treat this as their doing or as the island's. Say which, and I will spend my time accordingly.

interpretations.claim: They are doing it on purpose, and the water is the shape of how far they have got. If that is right, the spread is a map of their reach and we should be reading it as intelligence.
It is the island answering something, not a hand on a tap. If that is right, chasing the cult past the water wastes the little time we have, and I should be mapping the ground itself instead.
